title: There Was No Island Here. Just Sea. (Dubai, 2000-2003)
reel: No island. Just sea. Three years later: a palm tree, fully formed. Satellite images of Dubai's Palm Jumeirah, 2000-2003. #dubai #satellite #earthfromspace
description:
Between these two pictures: three years. NASA's ASTER satellite shows the same place off Dubai in 2000 and in 2003.
Images are false colour (plants appear red). Narration excerpt from our full video 'Dubai Islands'.

Credit: NASA Earth Observatory, World of Change (ASTER / Terra).
#Shorts #satellite #earth #dubai

limits: False-colour frames are labelled; frames are NASA's own framing, not re-registered by us. Sound checked by loudness meter and cue timetable, not by ear.

title: Great Salt Lake: 20+ Feet Below Its 1986 Record High
reel: 1986: record high, 4,211.6 ft. 2022: more than 20 feet lower. Same place, same satellite grid. #greatsaltlake #utah #climate
description:
The lake's record high came in 1986, at 4,211.6 feet. By July 2022 it sat more than 20 feet lower.
Landsat images on the same grid, so the wipe compares like with like. The amber line is the 1986 shoreline, traced from the same data.

Credit: Landsat imagery courtesy of the U.S. Geological Survey.
#Shorts #satellite #earth #greatsaltlake
limits: Strongest data story, least motion design: mostly one map.

origin: EP003 Great Salt Lake. Rebuilt 2026-10-21 with the original builder (gsl2); byte-identical to the 2026-10-15 record.
title: What the Great Salt Lake Left Behind
reel: When the water pulls back it leaves lake bed. Dust from the drying lake worsens regional air pollution (NASA). #greatsaltlake #saltlakecity #drought
description:
When the water pulls back, it leaves lake bed. NASA reports that dust from the drying Great Salt Lake worsens regional air pollution.
USGS measured arsenic, lead and cadmium in dust at 17 sites; health effects have not yet been formally evaluated (USGS).
The dust in the animation is an illustration, not a measured plume.

Credit: Landsat imagery courtesy of the U.S. Geological Survey; NASA; USGS.
#Shorts #satellite #earth #greatsaltlake
limits: Health topic: kept to the USGS wording. Amber fill is traced from the same stack and labelled; dust particles are labelled as illustration.

origin: EP004 Jakarta. NEW on 2026-10-21: cut from the approved EP004 episode (its own narration, no new voice) by yt-shorts/vshort.py; reframed to 1080x1920 with kinetic type.
title: Jakarta Is Sinking: Six Bowls, One at 7.7 cm a Year (Preprint)
reel: Count the hotspots a different way and Jakarta has six sinking bowls. The worst: up to 7.7 cm a year, about three inches. One preprint study. #jakarta #sinkingcity #satellite
description:
A separate study, still a preprint, combined radar and GPS from 2014 to 2025 and counted six main subsidence bowls. In the worst one, the vertical drop reached up to 7.7 centimeters a year, about three inches.
This is one study and it is not peer reviewed yet. The graphics are schematic illustrations, not map positions.

Full video: Jakarta Is Sinking: Satellites Reveal Why (OrbitalAtlas EP004).
Background: Landsat 8 imagery courtesy of the U.S. Geological Survey.
#Shorts #satellite #earth #jakarta
claims: EP004 claims C39 (and C05/C06 in the same passage), see EP004 story/claims.json
limits: Derived from the episode's own footage (schematics over a dimmed Landsat map), reframed; less cinematic than the native-vertical Shorts. Background is the same footage enlarged and blurred.

origin: EP004 Jakarta. NEW on 2026-10-21 (same method as Short 01).
title: How Fast Is Each Part of Jakarta Sinking? One Radar Study
reel: District by district: a 2019-2020 radar study reported 4.9 cm a year in North Jakarta, 4.8 West, 3.1 Central, 2.8 South, 2.5 East. #jakarta #sinkingcity #satellite
description:
A radar study of 2019 to 2020 reported average sinking rates of 4.9 centimeters a year in North Jakarta, 4.8 in West Jakarta, 3.1 in Central, 2.8 in the South and 2.5 in the East.
The abstract does not say whether these are line of sight or vertical. The sinking was mostly near the coast and river mouths, on soft river deposits.

Full video: Jakarta Is Sinking: Satellites Reveal Why (OrbitalAtlas EP004).
Background: Landsat 8 imagery courtesy of the U.S. Geological Survey.
#Shorts #satellite #earth #jakarta
limits: One study, rates not stated as line-of-sight or vertical (said on screen). Same reframing limits as Short 01.
